clue.text: Film one smashing up the bar

parts.note: to bar a way is to block it, used here as a noun phrase
a buster is someone or something that busts, i.e. smashes things up

explanation.surface: A movie about someone wrecking the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the reverse of clue order: BLOCK (bar) is written first, then BUSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge commercial hit movie is called a blockbuster, after the wartime bomb big enough to flatten a city block.

clue.text: Tree's position across motorway

indicators.note: the word for position stretches across, so the motorway letter sits inside it

parts.note: the lie of something is its position, as in the lie of the land
M is the standard abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Where a tree stands relative to a nearby motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree's' reads as 'Tree is': the definition followed by a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The linden, a broad-leaved shade species, is commonly known as the lime.

clue.text: Sponge, say — a piece is easy to get

definitions.text: a piece is easy to get

explanation.surface: A slice of sponge is simple to come by.
explanation.walkthrough: The second part leans on the idiom 'a piece of cake', meaning something very easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge is one kind of baked sweet treat; and the idiom 'piece of ...' means a task that is effortless.

clue.text: Bellow's odd biographer

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters of the novelist's name are strangely arranged

parts.note: the name Bellow with its possessive S, all seven letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: Saul Bellow's peculiar life-writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive S is part of the fodder here. James Boswell wrote the famous Life of Samuel Johnson.
explanation.definitionFit: James Boswell is the classic literary life-writer, author of the Life of Samuel Johnson.

clue.text: Sound of regret as vision stops short

indicators.note: stopping short means the word for vision loses its final letter

parts.note: sight is the faculty of vision

explanation.surface: A regretful noise made when one's eyesight starts failing.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhaling audibly is how people express sadness or disappointment.

clue.text: Require extremes of loyalty? Just so

parts.note: to exact something is to demand or require it

indicators.note: extremes of means the first and last letters of loyalty

explanation.surface: Asking whether total loyalty is demanded, and being told precisely that.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are emphatic agreements meaning precisely, quite right.

clue.text: Reach crisis, so approach senior teacher

explanation.surface: Things boil over, so one goes to see the head.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase means going up to a head teacher; idiomatically it means a situation reaching its climax.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a problem reaching its decisive point; literally it means approaching a school's principal.

clue.text: One giving accounts of society to Conservative bank clerk

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
a teller is a clerk who serves customers at a bank counter

explanation.surface: A clerk who reports on society matters to the Conservative party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accounts' suggests banking but here means narratives.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrator relates tales, which are accounts of events.

clue.text: Securely fasten length of cloth

explanation.surface: Fixing a roll of fabric in place.
explanation.definitionFit: To lock with a sliding bar is to fasten; a roll of fabric of standard length is also called by this name.

clue.text: Message of burning importance?

parts.note: a message sent by means of a fire, so literally burning, rather than one that is urgent

explanation.definitionFit: Native peoples sent communications with puffs from a fire, so the message really did involve burning.

clue.text: Insect goes to river for drink

parts.note: a bee is a stinging insect
R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A bug flies down to the water to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale and lager are alcoholic beverages of this type.

clue.text: Cooperating closely, giving affection

parts.note: handing something over is giving it
love is deep affection

explanation.surface: Working together in partnership while showing warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes two parties working in very intimate partnership, often conspiratorially.

clue.text: Country pursuits involving shedding?

parts.note: rural hunting activities, where the shedding is of the quarry's life fluid rather than of hair or leaves

explanation.definitionFit: Hunting, shooting and coursing are activities in which animals are killed, so their life fluid is spilt.

clue.text: In sum, there's no more to say

explanation.surface: A summing-up: everything has now been said.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in total; read literally it says everything has been recounted.

clue.text: Departs to the other side — from here?

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for departs on timetables
to go over is to cross to the other side

explanation.surface: Someone leaving for the Continent, setting off from this English port.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kent port of Dover is where ferries leave England for France across the Channel, so the whole clue paints the departure.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kent harbour town is Britain's main ferry departure point for crossings to France.

clue.text: At top speed on the level in the open air

parts.note: flat means level, without slopes
out means outdoors, in the open air

explanation.surface: Running as fast as possible on flat ground outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Going as fast as possible, with maximum effort, is an idiom used of runners and engines.

clue.text: Fast ships

explanation.surface: Speedy vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet-footed means swift; a navy's assembled vessels form this group.

clue.text: Money a sucker sees disappearing slowly

explanation.surface: Cash that a dupe watches dwindle gradually.
explanation.walkthrough: Lolly is British slang for money, and short for lollipop, a sweet on a stick that is sucked away bit by bit.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for cash; also a lollipop, which a licker watches shrink as it is sucked.

clue.text: Tiny bit of water in sink

explanation.surface: A small amount of water in a basin.
explanation.definitionFit: A single bead of liquid; and to fall or go down, as a price or ship can.

clue.text: Stuff read out by boy

indicators.note: read out signals that the word for stuff is spoken and spelt as it sounds

parts.note: to stuff something is to fill it

explanation.surface: Material read aloud by a young lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Phil, short for Philip, is a man's first name.

clue.text: As a Basque, it may go to one's head

definitions.text: As a Basque, it may go to one's head

parts.words: As a Basque, it may go to one's head
parts.note: the Basque type of soft flat cap worn on the head, with a hint of something going to one's head like drink

explanation.definitionFit: The round flat soft woollen cap is traditionally associated with the Basque country.

clue.text: Doctor's manner to one that's lying?

definitions.text: Doctor's manner to one that's lying?

parts.words: Doctor's manner to one that's lying?
parts.note: a physician's way with a patient lying in bed, playing on lying meaning telling untruths

explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's tact with patients is called a good ... manner, named for the place beside the patient's bed.

clue.text: Move emotions, receiving honour that's excessive

indicators.note: receiving means the word for moving emotions takes the honour inside it

parts.note: to touch someone is to move them emotionally
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Being moved to receive an award is overwhelming.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean more than is needed or reasonable.

clue.text: Have drunk retsina, not so nice

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of the wine are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: Drinking the Greek resinated wine makes one less pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of a word meaning unpleasant, i.e. less pleasant.

clue.text: All our ships can carry horse through sound

indicators.note: the horse goes through the word for sound, splitting it

parts.note: a tone is a musical sound
a nag is an old or poor horse

explanation.surface: A horse being carried across the strait by the fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: NAG goes between TON and E. 'sound' looks like a body of water but means a note.
explanation.definitionFit: The cargo capacity of a vessel or fleet is measured in this unit of weight.

clue.text: Look at good books for prize

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look, as in lo and behold
OT is the Old Testament, books of the Good Book

explanation.surface: Examining well-behaved records to win an award.
explanation.definitionFit: Plunder seized in war is taken as a prize or spoils.

clue.text: Mark left by damage to second vehicle

parts.note: a car is a motor vehicle

explanation.surface: A dent left after an accident to the family's second car.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasting blemish left after a wound heals.

clue.text: Wears a ritual piece of Hindu clothing

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone dons a garment for a religious ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: The draped length of cloth is a traditional garment of Indian women.

clue.text: Determined to be hard on one of Adam's boys

parts.note: set means determined, as in set on doing something
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Being firm about being tough on one of the first man's sons.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Adam's third son, born after Cain and Abel.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Adam and Eve's third son, born after Abel's murder.

clue.text: Depressed as our old record goes first

indicators.note: goes first moves the record ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
aged means old

explanation.surface: Feeling low because an old record of ours is played first.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists 'our old' before 'record', but 'goes first' puts DISC at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean disheartened, low in spirits.

clue.text: Refuse to allow doctor round

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A medic declining to permit a ward round.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbid or block a proposal is to exercise a right of rejection.

clue.text: Henry in clear sight, perhaps, lit by this?

indicators.note: in places Henry inside the rearranged letters
perhaps signals the words clear sight are to be taken loosely and rearranged

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry stands plainly visible, illuminated by a powerful lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside an anagram of CLEARSIGHT, signalled by 'perhaps'. 'this' stands for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerful beam lamp illuminates a target, so something caught in it is lit up.
